questions.question: If (a + b + c) = 12 and (a² + b² + c²) = 60, find the value of (a − b)² + (b − c)² + (c − a)².
questions.questionHtml: If (a + b + c) = 12 and (a² + b² + c²) = 60, find the value of (a − b)² + (b − c)² + (c − a)².
questions.solution:
(a − b)² + (b − c)² + (c − a)²
= 2(a² + b² + c² − ab − bc − ca)

(a + b + c)² = a² + b² + c² + 2(ab + bc + ca)
144 = 60 + 2(ab + bc + ca)
2(ab + bc + ca) = 84
ab + bc + ca = 42
now,
(a − b)² + (b − c)² + (c − a)² = 2(60 − 42)
= 2 × 18
= 36

questions.question: The radius of base of a solid cylinder is 12 cm and its height is 15 cm. It is melted and converted into small bullets. Each bullet is of same size. Each bullet consisted of two parts viz. a cylinder and a hemisphere on one of its base. The total height of bullet is 5 cm and radius of base is 3 cm. How many complete bullets can be obtained?
questions.questionHtml: The radius of base of a solid cylinder is 12 cm and its height is 15 cm. It is melted and converted into small bullets. Each bullet is of same size. Each bullet consisted of two parts viz. a cylinder and a hemisphere on one of its base. The total height of bullet is 5 cm and radius of base is 3 cm. How many complete bullets can be obtained?
questions.solution:
Volume of the larger cylinder = πr²h = π × 12² × 15 = 2160π

Bullet = Cylinder + Hemisphere

Radius = 3 cm, Total height = 5 cm

Height of cylindrical part = 5 − 3 = 2 cm

Volume of cylinder = π × 3² × 2 = 18π

Volume of hemisphere = (2/3)π × 3³ = (2/3)π × 27 = 18π

Volume of one bullet = 18π + 18π = 36π

Number of bullets = 2160π / 36π = 60

+10%, then -10%

Net change = -1%

Answer: 20,000

questions.question: Read the following paragraph and answer the given questions accordingly: The 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami was triggered by a massive undersea earthquake off the coast of Sumatra, registering a staggering magnitude. As the tectonic plates shifted violently, they displaced billions of tons of water, sending concentric ripples across the deep ocean at the speed of a jet aircraft. In the open sea, these waves remained deceptive—mere swells only a few feet high—allowing unsuspecting mariners to sail over them without realizing the impending doom racing toward the distant coastlines. However, as the energy reached the shallower coastal shelves, the phenomenon of "shoaling" occurred. The front of the wave slowed down due to friction with the seabed, while the back continued at high speed, forcing the water to wall up into terrifying heights. Eyewitnesses in Thailand and India described the initial retreat of the shoreline as a "hollowed-out" sea, luring curious onlookers toward the exposed seabed just moments before the crest slammed inland. The aftermath was a somber testament to nature’s caprice, leaving behind a trail of decimated infrastructure and shifted topographies. Q- According to the passage, why were mariners in the open sea unable to detect the tsunami?

questions.question: In the following question, a number is coded as two digits, where: The first digit is the remainder when the number is divided by 6. questions.questionHtml:
In the following question, a number is coded as two digits, where:
The first digit is the remainder when the number is divided by 6.
The second digit is the remainder when the number is divided by 9.

That is, if a number N is divided by 6 and gives remainder a, and by 9 gives remainder b, then the code is (a, b).

Example:
If N = 50
50 ÷ 6 → remainder 2
50 ÷ 9 → remainder 5
So, the code is (2, 5)

Which is the least number with the code (1, 4) in this coding system?
questions.solution:
21:
21 ÷ 6 = remainder 3 ❌
21 ÷ 9 = remainder 3 ❌

39:
39 ÷ 6 = remainder 3 ❌
39 ÷ 9 = remainder 3 ❌

27:
27 ÷ 6 = remainder 3 ❌
27 ÷ 9 = remainder 0 ❌

31:
31 ÷ 6 = remainder 1 ✔
31 ÷ 9 = remainder 4 ✔

👉 Only 31 satisfies both conditions
